files.src/codec_h264.c: h264_profiles: ConstrainedBaseline, Main, High, High10 — not Baseline or Extended

research.note: Five-vector feature inventory is taken from those published records. This experiment does not copy ITU/Fluster bitstreams.

invariants.text: FFmpeg n9.0.1 vaapi_profile_map has ConstrainedBaseline/Main/High/High10 only. Baseline (66) and Extended (88) never exact-match.
Without an exact match, allow_profile_mismatch keeps the last advertised mapped H.264 VA profile (High, if advertised) rather than a feature-safe subset.
FMO is declared in PPS num_slice_groups_minus1. An SPS-only detector cannot find it. FM1_FT_E introduces a later PPS with one extra slice group.

BA3_SVA_C (Extended, I/P/B, frame_mbs_only=1, no FMO) and MR2–MR5_TANDBERG (Baseline, I/P, frame_mbs_only=1, no FMO) are the profile-override class. Hardware checksums for those five stay in parent #37.
Do not advertise VAProfile Baseline or Extended. Do not enable allow_profile_mismatch by default. Remap only a stream whose scanned SPS/PPS/slice features fit Constrained Baseline or Main.

ff_profile from the first picture does not freeze the subset. Every later SPS is checked against the selected VA profile for profile_idc, bit depth and 4:2:0 chroma. A High 10 parameter-set change after Baseline is rejected, not kept as Constrained Baseline.
Baseline→Constrained Baseline allows I/P only. Extended→Main allows I/P/B only. SP and SI slices are outside every advertised subset and reject before the remap.

VA CreateConfig takes a VAProfile, not a feature inventory. FFmpeg decides the profile before later PPS changes. The installed client API cannot express this remap safely without a local FFmpeg change that inspects SPS+PPS and re-checks on parameter-set change.
